articleTitle: Exosomal Non-Coding RNAs in Gastrointestinal Cancer Drug Resistance: A Systematic Review of Emerging Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
takeaways: This systematic review analyzed 76 studies (50 cohort studies and 26 case-control studies) spanning from 1994 to 2025, identifying specific exosomal non-coding RNAs (microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and circular RNAs) as potential biomarkers for predicting gastrointestinal cancer drug resistance

Three main types of non-coding RNAs found in exosomes - microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs) - emerged as the most extensively studied molecules with both prognostic significance and predictive relevance for gastrointestinal cancer treatment outcomes

Despite extensive research across 76 studies over three decades, none of the identified exosomal biomarkers have progressed beyond preclinical studies to actual clinical use, indicating current limitations in translating this research into practical diagnostic tools

Exosomal non-coding RNAs show potential as dual-purpose biomarkers that can both predict treatment resistance and provide prognostic information for gastrointestinal cancers, though clinical validation and standardization remain major challenges
